attributes.mlflow.spanOutputs:
{"result": "1	# BlastNet → WELL format (example)
2	
3	This folder is a **small, self-contained copy** of two BlastNet dataset families plus the full `convert_to_well_format.py` used for the COMB-FLOW-UNI conversion pipeline. Use it to demo conversion for an agentic data team or to smoke-test the script without touching the full `blastnet_data` tree.
4	
5	## Layout
6	
7	```
8	Data_conversion_example/
9	  blastnet_data/                    # input (mirrors blastnet_data/<dataset>/...)
10	    lifted_hydrogen_jet/
11	      hydrogen-jet-5000/
12	      nonreacting-hydrogen-jet-5000/
13	    nonreacting_channel_flow/
14	      channelflow-dns-Re544-eq-p000-020/
15	      channelflow-dns-Re544-eq-p021-041/
16	  well_output/                      # default output HDF5 files (created by the script)
17	  convert_to_well_format.py
18	  submit_convert_to_well_example.sh # optional PBS job (edit project/queue)
19	  README.md
20	```
21	
22	## Original BlastNet layout (per trajectory)
23	
24	Each **trajectory** is a directory (for example `hydrogen-jet-5000/` or `channelflow-dns-Re544-eq-p000-020/`) containing:
25	
26	- **`info.json`** — metadata: `global.Nxyz` (grid size), snapshot count, variable list, paths to grid files, BC text, optional chemistry paths.
27	- **`data/*.dat`** — raw **float32** arrays, one file per field per time index (e.g. `P_Pa_id0000.dat`, `UX_ms-1_id0001.dat`). Names encode the physical quantity and units.
28	- **`grid/`** — `X_m.dat`, `Y_m.dat`, and for 3D cases `Z_m.dat` (float coordinates; the converter tries float32 then float64).
29	
30	The converter groups files by trajectory directory and field name, reads `info.json` for dimensions and time, maps BlastNet field names to WELL names, and writes a single HDF5 per trajectory.
31	
32	## WELL HDF5 layout (output)
33	
34	Each output file is named **`{dataset_name}_{traj_key}.hdf5`** (for example `lifted_hydrogen_jet_traj_5000.hdf5`, `nonreacting_channel_flow_traj_eq_020.hdf5`).
35	
36	Inside the file:
37	
38	- **Root attributes** — `dataset_name`, `grid_type`, `n_spatial_dims`, `n_trajectories`, etc.
39	- **`dimensions/`** — `time` (1D array of snapshot times), and `x` / `y` / (`z`) coordinate 1D arrays when grid files are present (otherwise normalized \([0,1]\) placeholder).
40	- **`boundary_conditions/`** — groups per BC type (periodic / wall / open) with masks; types come from `BC_MAPPINGS` in the script for each dataset family.
41	- **`t0_fields/`** — scalar fields (pressure, density, temperature, species mass fractions, …).
42	- **`t1_fields/`** — **`velocity`** as a vector field (stacked `UX`, `UY`, `UZ` when present).
43	- **`t2_fields/`** — reserved (empty in these conversions).
44	- **`scalars/`** — placeholder group for scalar parameters.
45	
46	Trajectory keys used in filenames (for `--only-trajectories`):
47	
48	| Dataset | Example subdirectory | Trajectory key |
49	|--------|----------------------|----------------|
50	| `lifted_hydrogen_jet` | `hydrogen-jet-5000` | `traj_5000` |
51	| `lifted_hydrogen_jet` | `nonreacting-hydrogen-jet-5000` | `traj_nonreacting_5000` |
52	| `nonreacting_channel_flow` | `channelflow-dns-Re544-eq-p000-020` | `traj_eq_020` |
53	| `nonreacting_channel_flow` | `channelflow-dns-Re544-eq-p021-041` | `traj_eq_041` |
54	
55	## Commands (interactive)
56	
57	From this directory, defaults are `--base-path ./blastnet_data` and `--output-path ./well_output`.
58	
59	**Dry run (no HDF5 written):**
60	
61	```bash
62	cd /lus/flare/projects/COMB-FLOW-UNI/Kiran/Data_conversion_example
63	
64	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset lifted_hydrogen_jet --dry-run
65	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset nonreacting_channel_flow --dry-run
66	```
67	
68	**Convert lifted hydrogen jet (both trajectories in this example):**
69	
70	```bash
71	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset lifted_hydrogen_jet
72	```
73	
74	**Convert channel flow (both trajectories):**
75	
76	```bash
77	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset nonreacting_channel_flow
78	```
79	
80	**Optional: single trajectory by key:**
81	
82	```bash
83	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset lifted_hydrogen_jet --only-trajectories traj_5000
84	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset nonreacting_channel_flow --only-trajectories traj_eq_020
85	```
86	
87	**Full BlastNet tree (not this example):** pass explicit paths, same as the original script:
88	
89	```bash
90	python3 convert_to_well_format.py --dataset premixed_flame_h2air \
91	  --base-path /lus/flare/projects/COMB-FLOW-UNI/blastnet_data \
92	  --output-path /lus/flare/projects/COMB-FLOW-UNI/blastnet_data/blastnet_data_well_format_complete
93	```
94	
95	## PBS batch job
96	
97	Edit account/queue paths in `submit_convert_to_well_example.sh`, then:
98	
99	```bash
100	qsub submit_convert_to_well_example.sh
101	```
102	
103	The job runs the two `--dataset` conversions sequentially and writes logs under this folder.
104	
105	## Resource note
106	
107	Channel-flow trajectories here are **very large** on disk (order \(10^2\) GB per case). Conversion loads time series into memory; run on a node with sufficient **RAM** and allow **long walltime**. Lifted-jet cases are smaller but still multi‑GB outputs.
108	
109	## Upstream reference
110	
111	The canonical copy of the converter (and the full converted HDF5 library) lives under:
112	
113	`/lus/flare/projects/COMB-FLOW-UNI/blastnet_data/convert_to_well_format.py`  
114	`/lus/flare/projects/COMB-FLOW-UNI/blastnet_data/blastnet_data_well_format_complete/`
115	
116	This example’s script is the same logic with **local default paths**, optional **`--only-trajectories`**, and the same **`--dataset`** / **`--dry-run`** interface.
117	"}

{"result": "1	# Data format
2	
3	The raw data of the Well are stored as HDF5 files, internally organized following a shared specification. The data stored in these files have been generated on uniform grids and sampled at constant time intervals. These files include all available state variables or spatially varying coefficients associated with a given set of dynamics in numpy arrays of shape (n_traj, n_steps, coord1, coord2, (coord3)) in single precision fp32. We distinguish between scalar, vector, and tensor-valued fields due to their different transformation properties.
4	
5	The specification is described below with example entries for a hypothetical 2D (D=2D=2) simulation with dimension B x T x W x H. Note that this uses HDF5 Groups, Datasets, and attributes (denoted by "@"):
6	```
7	root: Group
8	  @simulation_parameters: list[str] = ['ParamA', ...]
9	  @ParamA: float = 1.0
10	  ... # Additional listed parameters
11	  @dataset_name: str = 'ExampleDSet'
12	  @grid_type: str = 'cartesian' # "cartesian/spherical currently supported"
13	  @n_spatial_dims: int = 2 # Should match number of provided spatial dimensions.
14	  @n_trajectories: int = B # "Batch" dimension of dataset
15	
16	  -dimensions: Group
17	    @spatial_dims: list[str] = ['x', 'y'] # Names match datasets below.
18	    time: Dataset = float32(T)
19	      @sample_varying = False # Does this value vary between trajectories?
20	    -x: Dataset = float32(W) # Grid coordinates in x
21	      @sample_varying = False
22	      @time_varying = False # True not currently supported
23	    -y = float32(H) # Grid coordinates in y
24	      @sample_varying = False
25	      @time_varying = False
26	
27	  -boundary_conditions: Group # Internal and external boundary conditions
28	    -X_boundary: Group
29	      @associated_dims: list[str] = ['x'] # Defined on x
30	      # If associated with set values for given field.
31	      @associated_fields: list[str] = []
32	      # Geometric description of BC. Currently support periodic/wall/open
33	      @bc_type = 'periodic'
34	      @sample_varying = False
35	      @time_varying = False
36	      -mask: Dataset = bool(W) # True on coordinates where boundary is defined.
37	      -values: Dataset = float32(NumTrue(mask)) # Values defined on mask points
38	
39	  scalars: Group # Non-spatially varying scalars.
40	    @field_names: list[str] = ['ParamA', 'OtherScalar', ...]
41	    ParamA: Dataset = float32(1)
42	      @sample_varying = False # Does this vary between trajectories?
43	      @time_varying = False # Does this vary over time?
44	    OtherScalar: Dataset = float32(T)
45	      @sample_varying = False
46	      @time_varying = True
47	
48	  t0_fields: Group
49	    # field_names should list all datasets in this category
50	    @field_names: list[str] = ['FieldA', 'FieldB', 'FieldC', ...]
51	    -FieldA: Dataset = float32(BxTxWxH)
52	      @dim_varying = [ True  True]
53	      @sample_varying = True
54	      @time_varying = True
55	    -FieldB: Dataset = float32(TxWxH)
56	      @dim_varying = [ True  True]
57	      @sample_varying = True
58	      @time_varying = False
59	    -FieldC: Dataset = float32(BxTxH)
60	      @dim_varying = [ True  False]
61	      @sample_varying = True
62	      @time_varying = True
63	    ... # Additional fields
64	
65	  -t1_fields: Group
66	    @field_names = ['VFieldA', ...]
67	    -VFieldA: Dataset = float32(BxTxWxHxD)
68	      @dim_varying = [ True  True]
69	      @sample_varying = True
70	      @time_varying = True
71	    ... # Additional fields
72	
73	  -t2_fields: Group
74	    @field_names: list[str] = ['TFieldA', ...]
75	    - TFieldA: Dataset = float32(BxTxWxHxD^2)
76	      @antisymmetric = False
77	      @dim_varying = [ True  True]
78	      @sample_varying = True
79	      @symmetric = True # Whether tensor is symmetric
80	      @time_varying = True
81	    ... # Additional fields
82	```
83	"}

22	## Original BlastNet layout (per trajectory)
23	
24	Each **trajectory** is a directory (for example `hydrogen-jet-5000/` or `channelflow-dns-Re544-eq-p000-020/`) containing:
25	
26	- **`info.json`** — metadata: `global.Nxyz` (grid size), snapshot count, variable list, paths to grid files, BC text, optional chemistry paths.
27	- **`data/*.dat`** — raw **float32** arrays, one file per field per time index (e.g. `P_Pa_id0000.dat`, `UX_ms-1_id0001.dat`). Names encode the physical quantity and units.
28	- **`grid/`** — `X_m.dat`, `Y_m.dat`, and for 3D cases `Z_m.dat` (float coordinates; the converter tries float32 then float64).
29	
30	The converter groups files by trajectory directory and field name, reads `info.json` for dimensions and time, maps BlastNet field names to WELL names, and writes a single HDF5 per trajectory.
31	
32	## WELL HDF5 layout (output)
33	
34	Each output file is named **`{dataset_name}_{traj_key}.hdf5`** (for example `lifted_hydrogen_jet_traj_5000.hdf5`, `nonreacting_channel_flow_traj_eq_020.hdf5`).
35	
36	Inside the file:
37	
38	- **Root attributes** — `dataset_name`, `grid_type`, `n_spatial_dims`, `n_trajectories`, etc.
39	- **`dimensions/`** — `time` (1D array of snapshot times), and `x` / `y` / (`z`) coordinate 1D arrays when grid files are present (otherwise normalized \([0,1]\) placeholder).
40	- **`boundary_conditions/`** — groups per BC type (periodic / wall / open) with masks; types come from `BC_MAPPINGS` in the script for each dataset family.
41	- **`t0_fields/`** — scalar fields (pressure, density, temperature, species mass fractions, …).
42	- **`t1_fields/`** — **`velocity`** as a vector field (stacked `UX`, `UY`, `UZ` when present).
43	- **`t2_fields/`** — reserved (empty in these conversions).
44	- **`scalars/`** — placeholder group for scalar parameters.
